items.title: Quasi-regular and H1-regular sequences are preserved by base change when the quotient is flat
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the quasi-regular and H1-regular properties of a sequence are preserved under base change, assuming the quotient by the sequence is flat over the base. For the quasi-regular statement the proof observes that the associated graded pieces are direct sums of copies of the flat quotient, hence flat, deduces by induction and the flat short exact sequence lemma that all quotients by powers of the ideal are flat, and transfers the graded pieces to the base changed algebra using the identification of the power of the base changed ideal with the base change of the power. The H1-regular statement is read off from the corresponding vanishing statement for Koszul homology under base change.
